subject.title: Add Claw status and remove lifecycle

question: After the atomic deletion race is fixed, should OpenClaw adopt this stacked Claws lifecycle API and removal ownership model as the core implementation of the open RFC?
rationale: The line-level safety defect has a bounded repair, but the public CLI, persisted schemas, and ownership semantics are new core product contracts whose prerequisites are not on main.

options.title: Approve after atomic repair
options.body: Keep the status/remove design, require atomic unchanged-file deletion, and review the prerequisite stack in order.

options.title: Ship status first
options.body: Land read-only inspection while deferring destructive removal until its ownership and atomicity contracts are settled.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Keep the drafts unmerged until maintainers decide whether the Claws RFC should proceed in core.

recommendation.title: Approve after atomic repair
recommendation.body: Keep the status/remove design, require atomic unchanged-file deletion, and review the prerequisite stack in order.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current fs-safe integration and is the best available owner for the core boundary and product-direction choice.
